title: Microinjection Wound Assay and In vivo Localization of Epidermal Wound Response Reporters in Drosophila Embryos.
protocol: Collect adult flies, 2-3 days after eclosing.
Add 50 females and 25 males to an embryo collection cage.
Place a fresh apple juice agar plus yeast plate each morning for 3 days.
Cycle the flies on a 12 hr diurnal schedule in a 25 °C incubator (lights "ON" at 05:00 and lights "OFF" at 17:00).
In the afternoon of Day-3, place a fresh apple juice plus yeast agar plate on the cage.
Collect embryos for 2 hours.
Place a new yeast plate on the cage and save the 2-hour collection plate.
Store the collection plate for an additional 14 hours at 25 °C to age the embryos.
Gently remove embryos from collection plates using a paintbrush by adding 2-3 ml water to the plate and swirling.
Transfer water and embryos from the plate to nylon mesh and collection tube.
Soak the mesh covered end of the collection tube containing the embryos in bleach for 2 min.
Manually rotate the collection tube a couple of times during soaking to prevent clumping.
Rinse embryos with water 10 times.
Dry the mesh covered collection tube containing the dechorionated embryos on a paper towel.
Transfer approximately 50 embryos from nylon mesh to an agar plate using a dissecting needle.
Add green food coloring to the agar plate for contrast and aid in embryo alignment.
Arrange two parallel rows of about 25 embryos each on the agar plate, ensuring they are aligned at right angles to the puncture needle on the microinjection apparatus.
Leave approximately one embryo length space between embryos for gas exchange purposes.
Place a slide with double stick tape over the aligned embryos and carefully press the slide to transfer embryos from the green plate to the slide.
Air dry the embryos for about 25 minutes to reduce internal pressure and prevent bursting when wounded.
Place 2-3 drops of halocarbon oil mix over the embryos to prevent further dehydration.
Position the embryo slide on the injection microscope stage.
Find the embryos in the field of view under the inverted microscope.
Practice moving the stage of the microscope to efficiently wound aligned embryos.
Focus on the middle plane of the embryo along the dorsoventral axis before wounding.
Begin wounding the row closer to the needle apparatus first.
Carefully place and secure a pulled-needle in the needle holder.
Use the micromanipulator to move the needle down toward the slide.
Align the needle with the embryo in the same focal plane.
Move the stage to puncture the embryo through and through.
Move to the next embryo in the row after puncturing.
When done wounding the first row, use the micromanipulator to move the needle completely up and away from the stage.
Manually rotate the slide 180° before moving it.
Wound the second row of embryos.
Store the embryos under halocarbon oil at room temperature.
Proceed with embryo fixation if conducting in situ hybridization or antibody staining.
Alternatively, store the embryos for 4-6 hours under halocarbon oil.
For visualization of the fluorescent reporter, anesthetize the embryos using 50% 1-phenoxy-2-propanol.
Remove the embryos from the halocarbon oil and place them on a new slide.
Place glass beads around the embryos.
Add a few drops of the anesthetic to the embryos.
Place a cover slip on the embryos.
Load needle from the rear with 1 μl of chemical solution plus dye.
Allow capillary action to draw the chemical solution to the tip of the needle.
Place a cover slip at an angle on a slide and coat the edge with halocarbon oil mix.
Bring the mounted needle into focus with the edge of the angled cover slip.
Gently move cover slip edge across the tip of the needle until broken.
Apply pressure on microinjection apparatus and check that the chemical solution plus dye is flowing out the needle.
Place the slide containing aligned embryos on the microscope stage.
Focus the embryo and the needle in the same plane.
Simultaneously puncture and microinject chemical solution plus dye into each embryo.
Drain halocarbon oil mix from injection slides.
Rinse heptane over the slide and wash into a glass Petri dish.
Use a glass pipette to rinse embryos from the slide with heptane until all embryos are removed.
Transfer the heptane plus embryo solution from the glass dish into a 20 ml scintillation vial.
Shake the vial for 2-3 min, remove the heptane and add fresh heptane.
Add 5 ml of fresh fixation solution to the vial.
Cap the vial and attach it to an orbital platform shaker.
Shake the vial containing the embryos for 25 min at 220-230 rpm.
Let the bubbles at the interface pop after shaking stops.
Completely remove the bottom, aqueous phase with a pipette, avoiding pulling up the embryos.
Add 5 ml of methanol to the vial.
Cap the vial and shake vigorously by hand for 20-30 seconds.
Swirl the vial and place it on the bench.
Carefully remove the top heptane layer.
Add 5 ml of fresh methanol to the vial.
Shake the vial so that the embryos sink.
Remove the methanol plus embryo solution with a glass transfer pipette.
Collect the solution in a nylon mesh collection tube placed in a glass dish.
Remove the methanol from the embryos.
Rinse the embryos with 1x PBS solution.
Transfer the embryos from the nylon mesh to an apple juice plate.
Spread the embryos out along the surface of the plate.
Transfer the embryos to a double stick tape glass slide.
Cover the embryos with 1x PBS.
Carefully push the embryos with a dissecting needle to "pop" the vitelline membrane.
Transfer the 1x PBS plus embryos to a 1.5 ml tube using a glass pipette.
Rinse the embryos with 1x PBS and store at 4°C.
Proceed to dehydrate the embryos using an Ethanol:PBS series.
Continue with in situ hybridization or immunolocalization protocol.
